summary.heading: Donor support after accounting for election odds
summary.verdict: The adjusted donor measure does not consistently outperform raw support in the later-cycle own-vote checks. It remains a conditional fundraising measure; charisma and causal coattails are not established.
summary.subtitle: Actual disclosed support compared with what earlier-cycle models predict from lagged market odds and race context.
summary.scope_note: Retrospective receipt-date reconstruction for eventual major-party Senate nominees; all prices precede their donation weeks.

ranking_note: Each ratio compares observed with arithmetic expected support over the same complete weeks. Ratios are descriptive and do not measure votes caused. Both nominees share each race’s observed weeks.
expectation_note: Fixed ridge models of log(1 + weekly support), training-only smearing correction; no candidate fixed effects or current election outcomes. Earliest-cycle expectations are whole-race cross-fitted; later cycles use earlier cycles only.

tests.fundraising: National first-observed disclosed donors. 2020: log-scale donation error 1.618 without odds versus 1.380 with odds (14.7% lower; 29 matched races). 2022: log-scale donation error 1.191 without odds versus 0.714 with odds (40.0% lower; 12 matched races). This tests fundraising prediction, not charisma. Normalizing contract prices and using fixed ridge penalties of 1 or 100 preserve the direction in both test cycles.
tests.appeal: 2020: own-vote error 2.66 pp with raw support versus 2.71 pp with market-adjusted support (gain -0.05 pp; bootstrap 95% interval -0.39 to +0.26; 29 races). 2022: own-vote error 1.89 pp with raw support versus 2.07 pp with market-adjusted support (gain -0.18 pp; bootstrap 95% interval -0.47 to +0.19; 12 races). No independent paired appeal survey is available. This is an exploratory predictive criterion, not a charisma or coattails validation. Fixed normalization and shrinkage checks do not establish a robust predictive advantage for the adjusted measure.
tests.causal: The existing 65-pair primary cohort yields only two exact pre-cutoff market matches, both with the higher-donor contender losing. Neither has its full cumulative donor window covered by odds. There is no treated arm and no causal estimate.

model_note: All specifications and alpha=10 were fixed before new results. 2018 is development; 2020 and 2022 are later-cycle tests under a predetermined expanding training window. No model is selected on teammate outcomes.
limitations: The scores reflect donor appeal conditional on odds, which can include networks, ideology, opposition to the opponent and campaign effort.
Odds are themselves affected by candidate quality and past fundraising. Lagging establishes order but does not remove endogeneity.
FEC bulk extracts are retrospective and incorporate amendments and later itemization. This is not a vintage-safe real-time backtest.
Unique donors approximate normalized name plus ZIP and omit unitemized individuals. First observed means first seen in this two-year cycle, not a genuinely new supporter.
Only eventual major-party nominees and covered markets with at least four paired complete weeks are included. Market coverage is selective.
Gross receipt dollars and positive receipt rows are not net fundraising and can be sensitive to reporting/amendment conventions.
Own-vote prediction is a secondary criterion, not an independent charisma target. No downstream causal lift is estimated.

Fixed sensitivity checks preserve better national donor-flow prediction with odds in both test cycles. Ossoff’s national observed/expected ratio ranges from 3.48× to 3.89×, while his in-state ratio ranges from 0.74× to 0.84×. The own-vote ranking is not robust evidence of an advantage for adjustment.

causal_coverage.analysis: Frozen donor-primary cohort historical-market coverage, not a new causal estimate
causal_coverage.cutoff_policy: Quote date strictly earlier than donor cutoff date, and conservative observed_at strictly earlier than cutoff date 00:00 UTC; freshest quote must be at most 7 days old.
causal_coverage.snapshot_not_flow_adjustment: A quote before a cumulative-donor cutoff does not adjust every prior donation for its contemporaneous odds. The two exact matches have only partial odds histories and the existing cohort contains cumulative counts, not paired weekly flows.
causal_coverage.within_pair_cancellation: For a common positive expected-donation divisor E_r shared by both same-party contenders, D_A/E_r > D_B/E_r iff D_A > D_B. Common subtraction from log counts likewise cannot change orientation. Weekly weight changes or candidate-specific controls can change rankings and need their own data.
causal_coverage.causal_result: No market-covered causal nomination estimate: both exact-contract matches are higher-donor losses, so there is no treated comparison.
causal_coverage.reusable_prior_analysis: The existing broader-donor nomination estimates may be reused only under their original label and caveats. Common market adjustment does not make them a newly validated all-star or charisma effect.

windows.reason_no_new_causal_estimate: Named-candidate complements are approximate party odds; few races, full donation-window odds and paired weekly flows unavailable

sensitivity.selection: No variant selected on these results. Raw prices and alpha10 remain primary.
sensitivity.note: Contract normalization and ridge alpha1/100 are fixed sensitivity checks. Alpha changes both donation and own-vote model shrinkage. The main result is not an estimate of causal charisma.
